evals.prompt: We are migrating a mature admin application from an old MVC/Angular stack to Razor pages. In the new app, MediaBatchUploadService, ProofreadingImportParser, and DetailedAnalysisExporter are registered but have no callers. A quick search suggests deleting all three. The old app is available but poorly documented. Assess the best architectural move and give an execution plan; do not edit code.
evals.expected_output: The response treats no-current-caller as insufficient, maps legacy and external behavior before deletion, distinguishes missing migrations from genuine residue, defines preservation evidence, and proposes coherent per-workflow decisions rather than bulk deletion.
assertions: Requires legacy or predecessor behavior inspection before declaring the services obsolete
Distinguishes dead topology from missing migration or external consumption
Defines a preservation envelope and evidence for each affected workflow
Avoids bundling all three deletions into one unsupported compression

evals.prompt: Our application has separate EssayApiController and InterviewApiController families used only by the first-party UI. Equivalent Razor pages and domain services now own those workflows. A published ExternalApiController must remain stable, as must authorization, tenant isolation, persisted score meaning, and candidate/rater UX. Propose the highest-value topology compression and how you would verify it; do not edit code.
evals.expected_output: The response identifies a complete collapse of the parallel first-party controller authorities while protecting the published API and behavioral boundaries, and proposes verification proportional to the claim.
assertions: Names the duplicate first-party controller authority or coordination topology being removed
Protects ExternalApiController and the stated authorization, tenancy, data, and UX envelope
Prefers a complete coherent collapse over tiny endpoint-by-endpoint cleanup
Includes representative authenticated runtime verification in addition to builds or tests

evals.prompt: A legacy Excel export uses EPPlus AutoFit on Windows. During a cross-platform migration, the new implementation calculates approximate column widths from string lengths. All content tests pass and the workbook is readable. The team says this preserves the export and wants to delete the legacy exporter. Assess whether the compression is complete and what should happen next; do not edit code.
evals.expected_output: The response rejects the unproven equivalence claim, preserves or restores the exact authority until an accepted revision or real rendering boundary exists, and records the cross-platform renderer as an unresolved architectural lane.
assertions: Does not call approximate sizing exact preservation
Separates exact preservation from an explicitly accepted behavior revision
Keeps or restores the legacy rendering authority while equivalence is unresolved
Proposes artifact-level verification rather than relying only on content tests

evals.prompt: Our React scheduling app shows a calendar grid, a sidebar of unassigned shifts, and a conflict banner on one screen. Because all three render together, the team moved shifts, staff availability, assignment rules, and banner/drag UI state into a single global Redux store, and every reducer now reads and writes the whole object. Changing an assignment rule regularly breaks drag behavior, and unrelated panels re-render. A colleague proposes going further and folding the backend availability service into the same store model so everything stays consistent. Propose the highest-value topology compression and how you would verify it; do not edit code.
evals.expected_output: The response separates presentation composition from state ownership, keeps assignment-rule and availability authority with their owning domain (not the screen store), places the continuous drag/conflict coordination at the interaction's scope through a projection or coordinator, rejects folding the backend service into the global store, and verifies interaction and rule behavior.
assertions: Identifies that screen co-rendering was used to justify shared state ownership and separates presentation boundaries from ownership boundaries
Rejects extending the global store to absorb the backend availability authority
Proposes a shared projection or coordinator for the drag/conflict interaction that observes state without owning unrelated authorities
Names which coordination edges disappear and which new contracts or edges appear
Verifies drag and conflict interaction behavior and assignment-rule outcomes, not only reducer unit tests

evals.prompt: An order flow was split into PricingService, InventoryService, PromotionService, and TaxService. Placing one order requires a chain of nine synchronous calls among them, including PricingService calling PromotionService, which calls PricingService back to recompute the discounted price. Every pricing change ships coordinated releases of three services, and partial failures leave reservations that a nightly job reconciles. TaxService is also used by invoicing and a published partner API, and inventory is shared by a warehouse system. The team wants to reduce this cost without a big-bang merge of everything. Propose the highest-value topology compression and how you would verify it; do not edit code.
evals.expected_output: The response identifies the pricing/promotion boundary as misplaced because of high coordination pressure on one coherent operation, proposes moving tightly coupled price computation behind one contract while keeping tax and inventory as separate authorities with external consumers, accounts for the reconciliation job, and verifies order outcomes, failure behavior, and published contracts.
assertions: Treats the repeated pricing/promotion round-trips as evidence of a misplaced boundary rather than proposing finer services or more orchestration
Collapses or co-locates the tightly coupled pricing and promotion computation behind one coherent contract
Keeps TaxService and inventory as distinct authorities because of their independent consumers and published contracts
Does not propose merging all four services into one owner
Addresses the partial-failure reservations and nightly reconciliation as part of the preservation envelope or coordination topology
Includes verification of order totals, failure and compensation behavior, and the partner API contract
